concept.title: Paragraphs
concept.abstract:
This section covers the Paragraph style in DOCX— its role as the primary carrier of explanatory, introductory, and transitional prose in any technical document — and four scenarios: a paragraph in a concept topic, a paragraph containing mixed inline character styles, a paragraph placed before the first heading, and a code paragraph. The converter maps each paragraph to a

element inside the classified topic body, extracts the based on the paragraph context, and maps recognized inline character styles to their corresponding DITA inline elements.

conbody.p: Paragraphsare the fundamental unit of prose communication in any technical publication. They carry three types of content as described below:

ul.li: Explanatory content that defines concepts and terms
Introductory content that sets the context for the structured elements that follow such as list, workflows, tables, procedures, and images
Transitional content that connects sections and chapters through the document's logic

conbody.p: This prose content is essential not only for readability but for building complete technical context, search discoverability and structural completeness.
conbody.note: A topic consisting only of a list or a table, with no surrounding prose, is a valid but an incomplete piece of technical communication. It is recommended to add the context to such structured elements.
conbody.p:
In a .docx file, Normal and Body Text paragraphs appear between headings, list items, tables, and images. The converter maps each Normal or Body Text paragraph to a

element inside the classified topic body and evaluates the first paragraph in a section as a candidate when it forms one complete sentence. Empty paragraphs used for spacing are removed during conversion and produce no

element. Use paragraph spacing settings instead of blank paragraphs to control whitespace.

The converter identifies Normal and Body Text paragraphs by their style name in the document and maps each one to a

element inside the classified DITA topic body — , , or — preserving paragraph order and the inline character formatting of every run within it.
